title: Fra Guglielmo Vizani to the Comte de Césy, Prinkipo, 8 October 1637 (BnF Français 16158 f. 292)

steps.what: Email from Satoru (1 Oct 2026): transcription, key and reading of the cipher, with a page at satoru.net/crypt/vizani/.
Copied his 54-word sign transcription and sign-to-letter table into cipher_words.tsv and key.json.
Re-decoded all 54 words (dec.py): 46 agree with his plain, 2 differ (monsignor, a letter missing in his glyph string), the rest name codes or his queried words.
Italian letter score of the decode -1.78 per letter against a best of -4.30 over 200 shuffled keys of the same shape (it-cinquecento).
Compared a IIIF crop of the Gallica image with his glyphs: first nine words of line 1 and the code 64 before the second Monsignor Beria agree.
His own controls (16 synthetic ciphers, 24 shuffled texts, 5 of 8 seeds identical) and the f. 294 line read with the same key, taken from his page; not re-run.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Satoru's key (recovered ciphertext-only with Claude) was applied to his transcription here: 46 of 48 plain words agree, the decode scores -1.78 per letter against -4.30 for the best of 200 shuffled keys, and the first words check against the Gallica image.
outcome.notes: Name codes 31, 36, 64?, 198, 227, 231 unread (no code list known); two unread signs and one queried word. Identification of Beria with Kontaris is Satoru's.

credits.note: transcription, key and reading (with Claude), emailed and published; verified here

prior.where: satoru.net/crypt/vizani/ (published 1 Oct 2026), after this project listed the cipher as untranscribed

human: The owner forwarded the outside email of 1 Oct 2026 and asked the model to review, verify and write it up. No cryptanalysis was done here.
